prompt: A metal has a density of $7.8$ grams per cubic centimeter. What is the mass, in grams, of a $250$ cubic centimeter block of this metal?
hint: Density tells how many grams are in each cubic centimeter. Think about how to combine it with the volume to get a mass.

hints.text: Density tells how many grams are in each cubic centimeter. Think about how to combine it with the volume to get a mass.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try round numbers: at $2$ g per cm³, a $10$ cm³ block weighs $20$ g — you multiply. Density times volume gives mass, and the cm³ units cancel to confirm it.
Every one of the $250$ cubic centimeters has a mass of $7.8$ grams, so multiply: $7.8 \times 250$.
Since $7.8 \times 250 = 1950$, the mass of the block is $1950$ grams.

learningObjective: Apply a density rate to compute a total.
explanation: Density is mass divided by volume, so mass equals density times volume.
Multiply the density by the volume: $7.8 \times 250 = 1950$. The cubic centimeters cancel and leave grams.
The mass of the block is $1950$ grams.

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate to check the magnitude
steps: Round the density up to $8$ grams per cubic centimeter, which gives about $8 \times 250 = 2000$ grams.
The rounding added $0.2$ grams for each of the $250$ cubic centimeters, which is $0.2 \times 250 = 50$ grams too many.
Removing that excess from the estimate gives the exact mass, $2000 - 50 = 1950$ grams.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Dividing $250$ by $7.8$ gives about $32$, far too light for a metal block of this size.
The units show the right operation: grams per cubic centimeter times cubic centimeters leaves grams.
So the two numbers must be multiplied, and $7.8 \times 250 = 1950$ grams.
